title: South32 sees limited risk of Indonesia replicating nickel success in alumina

title: Indonesia Aims to Dominate Global Nickel Supply Chain Amid Smelter Expansion and Price Forecasts
body: APNI’s Meidy Katrin Lengkey highlighted Indonesia’s 414,000‑ton nickel consumption and 54 operating smelters (plus 49 under construction and 5 export‑focused) as the country positions itself to meet a projected 700‑million‑ton smelter demand this year, while warning of raw‑material shortages and a shift from a three‑year to a one‑year RKAB cycle. She projected next‑year nickel‑based product prices at $15,000–$16,000 per ton and urged government action to keep costs competitive and secure the full value chain from NPI and MHP to EV battery production.

title: Indonesia's B40 Biodiesel Policy Faces Challenges in Nickel Mining Sector
body: A government forum led by the EBTKE Director General highlighted that the 40% biodiesel mandate has added 3–5% production costs to nickel mining, amid a 15‑thousand‑per‑ton drop in nickel prices and new export and tax regulations. Stakeholders called for quarterly evaluations, supply‑chain safeguards, and policy flexibility to address upcoming B50 considerations and prevent operational disruptions.

title: Indonesia Nickel Price Index Shows Stable Nickel Prices, but MHP Prices Surge Amid EV Battery Demand
body: The INPI/Shanghai Metals Market report for September 1, 2025 indicates that nickel ore prices (1.2% CIF at $23.5–$25.5/mt, 1.6% CIF at $50.5–$53.8/mt) and downstream products such as NPI ($115.5/mt FOB) and high‑grade matte ($13,260/mt) remain unchanged, while Mixed Hydroxide Precipitate (MHP) prices jump $97 to $12,883/mt FOB, reflecting heightened demand from Asia’s EV battery sector. This price spike suggests that nickel downstream operators will increasingly prioritize MHP and other high‑value products as the clean‑energy transition accelerates.
